scene.content: 十五夜の宵、若い尼たち、仏に花を供え、端近くいる女三の宮、鈴虫の声に耳を傾ける。
scene.contenten: On the night of the full moon the young nuns offer flowers to the Buddha; the Third Princess, near the edge, listens to the bell crickets.

scene.content: 女三の宮を訪れた源氏、琴を弾く。 奥では若い尼たち、仏壇供養。そこへ殿上人たちも集まってきて、鈴虫の宴となる。
scene.contenten: Genji, visiting the Third Princess, plays the koto; within, the young nuns make offerings at the altar; courtiers gather and it becomes a bell-cricket banquet.

scene.content: そこへ殿上人たちも集まってきて、鈴虫の宴となる。
scene.contenten: Courtiers also gather there, and it becomes a bell-cricket banquet.

scene.content: 同夜、源氏や集まっていた公達ら、冷泉院の月見の宴に招かれる。源氏と冷泉院、月光の下で語り合う。
scene.contenten: The same night, Genji and the noblemen gathered are invited to Emperor Reizei's moon-viewing banquet; Genji and Reizei talk under the moonlight.

summaryen: Genji dedicates the Buddhist image for the tonsured Onna San no Miya. On a moonlit autumn evening, he listens to bell-crickets released in her garden and plays the zither before visiting Retired Emperor Reizei for an intimate conversation late into the night. Troubled that her mother Rokujo's wandering spirit finds no peace, Empress Akikonomu considers taking holy vows, but Genji dissuades her, sponsoring elaborate sutra-reading assemblies to pray for Rokujo's soul.

title: 夕霧
summary: 落葉の宮への思慕を募らせた夕霧は小野の山荘へ押し掛け想いを打ち明けるが、宮は頑なに拒絶する。心痛のあまり母御息所が急死し、世間の浮名に絶望した落葉の宮は籠居するが、夕霧は強引に一条宮に移して契りを結ぶ。嫉妬に狂った正妻・雲居の雁は子らを連れて実家へ帰ってしまう。夕霧は二人の妻の間で板挟みとなりながらも、一門の重鎮として栄華を築いていく。
gendaibun: 一条の御息所がお亡くなりになってから、落葉の宮のお悲しみはいかばかりであったろう。小野の山里の秋風は冷ややかに吹き抜けて、世を頼りなく思われる日を送っておられた。
gendaibunen: How boundless was the grief of the Fallen Leaves Princess after the passing of the Ichijo Consort; the autumn winds swept coldly through the mountain hamlet of Ono, leaving her days solitary and unprotected.
kobun: 一条の御息所かくれ果てたまひて後、宮の御心細さ、言ひ尽くすべきならず。小野の山風も吹きまさりて、世をはかなう思さるるに。
kobunen: After the Ichijo Consort passed away, the Princess's loneliness was beyond words; the mountain winds of Ono raged cold, plunging her into despair.

scene.content: 小野の山荘を訪れ、以前からの思慕の情を落葉の宮に打ち明けた夕霧、宮の居室に入り、逃れようとする宮の御衣の裾を捉える。
scene.contenten: Yugiri, visiting the Ono villa, confesses his long-held love to the Lady Ochiba, enters her room, and catches the hem of her robe as she tries to flee.

scene.content: 自邸で、一条御息所の文を読む夕霧に雲居雁忍びより手紙を奪う。
scene.contenten: At his own residence, as Yugiri reads the Ichijo Lady Mother's letter, Kumoi no Kari steals up and snatches it.

scene.content: 翌朝、雲居雁の隠した文を探す夕霧。 室内で子供たち騒ぐ。
scene.contenten: The next morning Yugiri searches for the letter Kumoi no Kari hid; the children make a racket in the room.

scene.content: 小野の山荘の妻戸のわきに立つ夕霧、秋の夕陽に扇をかざす。垣の外には鹿が鳴いている。
scene.contenten: Standing by the door of the Ono villa, Yugiri holds a fan up to the autumn sunset; a deer cries beyond the fence.

scene.content: 致仕の大臣の文を持ち、蔵人少将(柏木の弟)、 落葉の宮を訪れる。
scene.contenten: Bearing a letter from the retired Minister, Kurando no Shosho (Kashiwagi's younger brother) visits the Lady Ochiba.

summaryen: Yugiri pursues Ochiba no Miya to her mountain retreat at Ono, but she resists his overtures. Heartbroken over the gossip, Ochiba's mother passes away. Despite the princess's grief, Yugiri forcibly consummates the union, prompting a furious Kumoi no Kari to flee back to her father's house with their children. Torn between the two women, Yugiri nonetheless secures his stature as a court pillar.

title: 御法
summary: 病の癒えない紫の上はたびたび出家を願うが、源氏は愛着の深さゆえに許さない。紫の上はせめてもの願いとして法華経千部供養を営み、明石の中宮や孫の匂宮に別れを告げる。秋風の立つ夕暮れ、露のように儚く息を引き取り、源氏は生涯最大の悲嘆に打ちひしがれ、後を追いたい絶望の中で野辺送りを営む。
gendaibun: 紫の上の御病気はその後も一向に快復に向かわれず、年を追って弱り衰えていかれるのを、源氏の大臣は何としても堪えがたく悲しく思っておられた。
gendaibunen: Murasaki no Ue showed no sign of recovery from her persistent illness; seeing her weaken year by year filled Lord Genji with unbearable anguish.
kobun: 紫の上の御心地、例ならずなりたまひて後、年を追ひて弱りたまふを、大臣、世に堪へがたく思し嘆く。
kobunen: After Murasaki no Ue fell ill, her health declined year after year, causing the Minister unendurable sorrow.

scene.content: 三月、紫の上の中宮、匂宮らを連れて紫の上を見舞う。紫の上、匂宮に庭前の紅梅と桜をこの後も慈しんでいくれるよう頼む。
scene.contenten: In the third month the Empress Murasaki visits Murasaki with Prince Niou and others; Murasaki asks Prince Niou to cherish the red plums and cherries in the garden hereafter.

scene.content: 夏、明石の中宮、匂宮らを連れて紫の上を見舞う。紫の上、匂宮に庭前の紅梅と桜をこの後も慈しんでくれるように頼む。
scene.contenten: In summer the Akashi Empress visits Murasaki with Prince Niou and others; Murasaki asks Prince Niou to cherish the garden's red plums and cherries hereafter.

scene.content: 秋の夕暮れ、重病の紫の上、風に吹かれる前栽を見て、源氏・明石の中宮と歌を交わす。
scene.contenten: On an autumn evening the gravely ill Murasaki, seeing the garden plants blown by the wind, exchanges poems with Genji and the Akashi Empress.

summaryen: Failing in health, Murasaki repeatedly pleads to become a nun, but Genji's passionate attachment refuses permission. She sponsors an offering of a thousand copies of the Lotus Sutra, bidding farewell to the Akashi Empress and young Niou. On an autumn evening, like vanishing dew, Murasaki breathes her last, plunging Genji into a despair so profound he longs to follow her into death.

title: 幻
summary: 最愛の紫の上を失った源氏は、二条院に閉じこもり四季の移ろいの中でただ亡き人を追慕する。新年の参賀も断り、蛍兵部卿宮や親しい人々の弔問にも上の空で過ごす。一年の服喪が明ける冬、源氏は紫の上から送られた文や数々の手紙を火にくべて焼き捨て、俗世との絆を断ち切って出家への決意を静かに固める。
gendaibun: 年が改まっても、源氏の大臣の御心は少しも晴れることがなく、二条院の御簾の内に引き籠もられたまま、参賀の人々にも一切お会いにならなかった。
gendaibunen: Even as the New Year turned, Lord Genji's heart found no solace; staying secluded behind the blinds of the Nijo mansion, he refused to receive any New Year visitors.
kobun: 年返りぬれど、大臣、なほ御心晴れず、二条の院に籠もりおはして、年賀の人々にも対面したまはず。
kobunen: Though the year had turned, the Minister's sorrow remained unlifted; remaining secluded at Nijo, he granted audience to none of his New Year callers.

scene.content: 紫の上を失った翌春、悲しみにくれる源氏は御簾の内に籠もり、参賀の人々にも会わず、 螢兵部卿宮とのみ歌を交わす。宮、紅梅の下に歩み出る。
scene.contenten: The spring after losing Murasaki, grieving Genji stays behind the blinds, sees no New Year visitors, and exchanges poems only with Hotaru Hyobukyo no Miya, who steps out beneath the red plums.

scene.content: 晩春、二条院の桜の盛りに紫の上を想い嘆く源氏。紫の上遺愛の桜を散らすまいとする匂宮の無邪気さに慰められる。
scene.contenten: In late spring Genji longs and grieves for Murasaki amid the blooming cherries of Nijo-in; he is comforted by Prince Niou's innocence in not letting Murasaki's beloved cherries scatter.

scene.content: 源氏、六条院の女三の宮を訪ねる。匂宮も侍女に抱かれて来、幼い薫と遊ぶ。 女三の宮、仏前で読経する。
scene.contenten: Genji visits the Third Princess at Rokujo-in; Prince Niou also comes in a lady's arms and plays with young Kaoru; the Third Princess chants sutras before the Buddha.

scene.content: 源氏、紫の上の残した文を読んで泣き、歌を書きつけてから皆焼いてしまう。
scene.contenten: Genji reads the writings Murasaki left, weeps, writes a poem, and then burns them all.

scene.content: 御仏名の導師の僧を、源氏ねぎらう。咲き始めた梅の花に雪。
scene.contenten: Genji thanks the officiating monk of the Buddha-name service; snow falls on the plum blossoms just beginning to open.

summaryen: Following Murasaki's death, Genji spends a year of solitary mourning at Nijo mansion, watching the seasons pass in acute grief. He declines official visitors, finding small comfort only in young Niou's innocence. At year's end, after burning Murasaki's letters to sever all remaining worldly attachments, Genji prepares to leave the world behind for good.

title: 匂宮
summary: 光源氏の没後、都では源氏の孫にあたる今上帝の三の宮（匂宮）と、柏木の実子でありながら源氏の次男として育てられた薫の二人が貴公子の双璧として名声を博す。生来の芳香を放つ薫に対し、対抗して名香を焚きしめる匂宮。出家の志を抱き物静かな薫と、華やかで好色な匂宮という対照的な二人の青年像が描かれる。
gendaibun: 光る源氏がこの世を去られてから、世の中の光が消え失せてしまったようで、誰も彼もが心細く寂しい思いに沈んでいた。
gendaibunen: After Shining Genji passed away from this world, it seemed that the light had vanished from society, plunging everyone into desolate loneliness.
kobun: 光る源氏失せたまひて後、世の中の光隠れたる心地して、人々あたらしき御形見を思ひ嘆く。
kobunen: After Shining Genji departed this world, the light seemed lost to the land, and all people grieved over the memory of his vanished glory.

scene.content: 正月十八日、弓場殿で賭弓。
scene.contenten: On the eighteenth day of the first month, an archery contest at the Yuba-den.

scene.content: 夕霧の催す賭弓の還饗に、匂宮・薫ら車を連ね、六条院へ。雪降る。
scene.contenten: At the banquet of the archery contest hosted by Yugiri, Prince Niou, Kaoru, and others line up their carriages and go to Rokujo-in; snow falls.

scene.content: 梅薫る下で六条院の還饗。女房ら物陰より覗き見る。
scene.contenten: A banquet at Rokujo-in beneath fragrant plums; ladies peek from the shadows.

summaryen: Years after Genji's passing, court society revolves around two young nobles: Prince Niou (Genji's grandson) and Kaoru (officially Genji's younger son, but secretly Kashiwagi's). While Kaoru emits an innate bodily fragrance, Niou rivals him by scenting robes with heavy incenses. Introspective Kaoru harbors thoughts of renouncing the world, in sharp contrast to the flamboyant, amorous Niou.

title: 紅梅
summary: 故頭中将の次男・按察大納言（紅梅）は、先妻との娘・大君を皇太子へ入内させ、後妻（真木柱）の連れ子・宮の姫君や実子の中の君の将来を思案する。大納言は風流な匂宮に紅梅の枝を添えて中の君への求婚を促すが、匂宮はむしろ未亡人・真木柱の連れ子である美しい宮の姫君に心を奪われ、大納言の思惑は外れていく。
gendaibun: 按察の大納言は、故致仕の大臣の御子でいらっしゃり、一族の中でも重んじられ、公私ともに栄えてお暮らしであった。
gendaibunen: The Azechi Dainagon, being the son of the late retired Chancellor, was held in high esteem throughout the lineage and enjoyed great prosperity both publicly and privately.
kobun: 按察の大納言は、故致仕の大臣の御子にて、世のおぼえも重く、公私につけて栄えたまへり。
kobunen: The Azechi Dainagon, a son of the late retired Chancellor, was highly honored at court and enjoyed splendid private and public fortunes.

scene.content: 按察大納言、参内しようとする直衣姿の若君に笛の稽古をさせる。奥にいる宮の姫君にも琵琶を合わせるよう勧める。
scene.contenten: The Azechi Dainagon has the young lord in noshi, about to go to court, practice the flute; he urges the princess of the household within to join on the biwa.

scene.content: 大納言、紅梅の枝に文をつけ、宮中の匂宮に届けるようにと若君に言いつける。
scene.contenten: The Dainagon attaches a letter to a red plum branch and orders the young lord to deliver it to Prince Niou in the palace.

scene.content: 若君、明石の中宮のもとにいる匂宮に、文と紅梅の枝を渡す。
scene.contenten: The young lord gives the letter and red plum branch to Prince Niou at the Akashi Empress's.

summaryen: Kashiwagi's brother, the Kobai Dainagon, seeks advantageous marriages for his daughters, sending Prince Niou a sprig of red plum blossom to encourage courtship of his second daughter. However, the amorous Niou sets his sights instead on Kobai's attractive stepdaughter (Makibashira's daughter), complicating the father's marital schemes.

title: 竹河
summary: 髭黒太政大臣の死後、未亡人となった玉鬘は二人の姫君（大君・中の君）の縁談に苦慮する。冷泉院や今上帝、夕霧の息子・蔵人少将らが求婚する中、源氏亡き後の重鎮となった薫は出家の思いを抱き静観する。結局、大君は高齢の冷泉院へ輿入れし、取り残された少将は中の君と結ばれるが、かつて玉鬘が誇った六条院の華やぎは薄れゆく。
gendaibun: 故髭黒の太政大臣が亡くなって後、玉鬘の北の方は、残された大君と中の君の行く末について、日夜心を砕いておいでになった。
gendaibunen: After the passing of the late Grand Chancellor Higekuro, his widow Tamakazura worried constantly day and night over the future of her two daughters, Oigimi and Naka no Kimi.
kobun: 故大将殿亡せたまひて後、北の方、姫君たちの御前を、いかがすべきと思し嘆く。
kobunen: After the late Chancellor died, his widow Tamakazura brooded anxious over what might become of her daughters' futures.

scene.content: 薫、早春の玉鬘邸で梅に鳴く鶯を聞き、女房たちと歌を詠み交わす。
scene.contenten: Kaoru, at Tamakazura's residence in early spring, hears a warbler singing on the plum and exchanges poems with the ladies.

scene.content: 梅の盛りの玉邸で薫、 蔵人少将に会う。 奥では女房たち、琵琶や箏を弾く。
scene.contenten: At Tamakazura's residence in plum season, Kaoru meets Kurando no Shosho; within, the ladies play the biwa and koto.

scene.content: 玉鬘の姫君たち、庭の桜を賭けて碁を打つ。勝ち方の童女、庭におりて花を拾う。蔵人少将このようすを覗き見る。
scene.contenten: Tamakazura's daughters play go wagering on the garden cherries; the winning girl goes into the garden to pick flowers; Kurando no Shosho peeks at this.

scene.content: 晩春の夕、冷泉院の庭で松にかかる藤を、薫、藤侍従とともに眺める。
scene.contenten: On a late-spring evening, in Emperor Reizei's garden, Kaoru and Fuji no Chujo gaze at wisteria on a pine.

summaryen: Following Chancellor Higekuro's death, Tamakazura faces dilemmas over marrying off her two daughters. Despite passionate suits from suitors including Yugiri's son Kurando no Shosho, the elder daughter enters the palace of the aging Retired Emperor Reizei, leaving the distraught young courtier to marry the younger sister instead.

title: 橋姫
summary: 桐壺帝の八男・八の宮は世を捨て宇治の山荘で二人の娘（大君・中君）と仏道に励んでいた。自らの出生の秘密に悩み世俗を嫌う薫は、宮を師と仰ぎ宇治に通い詰める。秋の有明の月夜、薫は合奏する姉妹の姿を垣間見て長女・大君に深く心を奪われる。老女房の弁の尼から、薫は自らの実父が柏木であることを明かされ、父の遺文を手渡されて激しい衝撃を受ける。
gendaibun: そのころ、世間から忘れられたように暮らしておられる古い親王がおいでになった。桐壺帝の第八の皇子でいらっしゃり、宇治の山里にひっそりと隠れ住んでおられた。
gendaibunen: In those days there lived an old prince whom the world seemed to have forgotten; he was the eighth son of the Kiritsubo Emperor, living in quiet seclusion in the mountain hamlet of Uji.
kobun: そのころ、世にかずまへられたまはぬ古宮おはしけり。桐壺の帝の八の宮にて、宇治の山里に隠れ住みたまふ。
kobunen: At that time there lived an aged prince forgotten by the world; he was the Eighth Prince of the Kiritsubo Emperor, dwelling in seclusion at Uji.

scene.content: 九月、薫、霧深く木の茂る山路を馬で宇治八の宮のもとに向かう。
scene.contenten: In the ninth month Kaoru rides along a misty, tree-grown mountain road toward the Eighth Prince at Uji.

scene.content: 宇治の中の君、さしでた月を揆で招き、大君、琴をひきさして笑う。薫、有明の月に照らされた姉妹を垣間見る。
scene.contenten: The middle sister at Uji invites the rising moon with a cup, and the eldest plays the koto and laughs; Kaoru glimpses the sisters lit by the moon at dawn.

scene.content: 改めて案内を乞うた薫、姫君たちのいる御簾の前に座り、物語をする。弁の御許、姫君の代わりに応対。
scene.contenten: Kaoru, asking to be guided again, sits before the blinds where the princesses are and talks; Ben no Okina answers for the princesses.

scene.content: 十月、八の宮、薫を迎えて琴を弾き、薫は琵琶を合わす。
scene.contenten: In the tenth month the Eighth Prince receives Kaoru and plays the koto; Kaoru joins on the biwa.

scene.content: 八の宮、 暁の勤行に立ったあと、薫、弁の御許より柏木と女三の宮の秘密を聞き、文反故を受け取る。
scene.contenten: After the Eighth Prince rises at dawn for devotions, Kaoru hears from Ben no Okina of the secret between Kashiwagi and the Third Princess and receives paper scraps.

summaryen: At Uji, the Eighth Prince lives in pious Buddhist seclusion with his two daughters, Oigimi and Naka no Kimi. Kaoru frequents the mountain villa seeking religious instruction, but on an autumn night he catches sight of the sisters playing music and falls in love with Oigimi. An old waiting woman, Ben no Ama, discloses the secret of Kaoru's illicit paternity by Kashiwagi, giving him his true father's hidden letters.

title: 椎本
summary: 薫に宇治の話を聞いた匂宮は興味を抱き、春の宇治を訪れて次女・中君と和歌を贈答する。秋、自らの死期を悟った八の宮は薫を呼び、姫君たちの後見を懇願してこの世を去る。薫は大君に求愛するが、大君は父の遺言を守って独身を通そうとし、むしろ薫には妹・中君と結ばれることを望む。薫の純粋で不器用な恋情は拒絶の中で深まっていく。
gendaibun: 年が明けて春になると、匂宮は薫が宇治の姫君たちのことを隠しているのを恨めしくお思いになり、初瀬参詣の折に宇治の山荘へ立ち寄られた。
gendaibunen: When spring arrived in the new year, Prince Niou, suspecting Kaoru was concealing the Uji princesses, stopped by their rustic villa on his way to Hase-dera.
kobun: 春になりて、匂宮、薫の中将の宇治の御ことを隠したまふを怨めしう思して、初瀬詣でのついでに立ち寄らせたまふ。
kobunen: In spring, Prince Niou, resenting that Kaoru kept the Uji ladies secret, took the occasion of a pilgrimage to Hase to stop at their mountain residence.

scene.content: 春、夕霧の宇治山荘で薫、匂宮ら宴遊。対岸の八の宮より薫に文届く。
scene.contenten: In spring at Yugiri's Uji villa, Kaoru and Prince Niou feast and amuse themselves; a letter from the Eighth Prince on the opposite shore reaches Kaoru.

scene.content: 招かれた公達ら船で八の宮の山荘に向かう。 船中で管弦。
scene.contenten: The invited noblemen go by boat to the Eighth Prince's villa, making music aboard.

scene.content: 月の明るい秋の夜、訪ねてきた薫に、自らの死を予感した八の宮、姫君たちのことを託す。
scene.contenten: On a moonlit autumn night the Eighth Prince, sensing his own death, entrusts his daughters to the visiting Kaoru.

scene.content: 歳の暮れ近く、宇治の姫君たちのもとに山の阿闍梨より炭などが届けられる。 姫君たちは綿、絹を贈る。
scene.contenten: Near year's end, charcoal and such arrive from the mountain acarya for the Uji princesses; they give cotton and silk in return.

scene.content: 薫、故八の宮の仏間に入り宮の生前を回想して柱にもたれ歌を詠む。女房ら、その姿を覗き見る。
scene.contenten: Kaoru enters the late Eighth Prince's Buddha room, recalls the prince's life, leans on a pillar and composes a poem; the ladies peek at him.

summaryen: Intrigued by Kaoru's accounts, Niou visits Uji and exchanges poetic verses with Naka no Kimi. In autumn, the Eighth Prince passes away after entrusting his orphaned daughters to Kaoru. While Kaoru presses his courtship upon Oigimi, she resolutely refuses marriage, wishing instead that Kaoru would take her younger sister Naka no Kimi as his wife.

title: 総角
summary: 八の宮の一周忌を機に薫は大君へ激しく想いを迫るが拒まれ、中君との結婚を斡旋される。薫は大君への誠意を示すため匂宮を手引きして中君と結ばせる。しかし匂宮の宇治通いは六条院の母・明石中宮の制止で途絶えがちになり、妹の不遇を嘆いた大君は自責の念から食を断って衰弱。最期まで貞潔を守り、薫の手の中で息を引き取る。薫は宇治川のほとりで絶望に沈む。
gendaibun: 八の宮の一周忌の御仏事も過ぎて、秋風が吹き立つころ、宇治の姫君たちの暮らしはいよいよ心細いものとなっていた。
gendaibunen: When the first anniversary services for the Eighth Prince had passed and autumn winds began to blow, the life of the Uji sisters became ever more forlorn.
kobun: 八の宮の一周忌の御事果てて後、秋風吹き立つころほひ、宇治の山里はいとど心細げなり。
kobunen: After the first anniversary of the Eighth Prince, with the onset of autumn winds, the mountain retreat of Uji appeared increasingly desolate.

scene.content: 宇治の秋の夜、薫、屏風を押し開け、執拗に大君に迫るが、つれなく拒まれる。
scene.contenten: On an autumn night at Uji, Kaoru pushes open a screen and persistently presses the eldest sister, but is coldly refused.

scene.content: 匂宮、薫とともに勾欄により遣水に月の映る秋の庭を眺め、宇治の姫君たちへの想いを語り合う。
scene.contenten: Prince Niou and Kaoru, leaning on the balustrade, view the autumn garden with the moon reflected in the stream and speak of their feelings for the Uji princesses.

scene.content: 匂宮、中の君と明けゆく宇治川を眺める。霧立ち、柴を積んだ舟が川面を行き交う。
scene.contenten: Prince Niou and the middle sister watch the Uji River at dawn; mist rises and boats piled with brushwood pass on the water.

scene.content: 十月、匂宮と薫ら、宇治川に舟を浮かべて紅葉狩り。 八の宮の山荘より女たちそのさまを眺める
scene.contenten: In the tenth month Prince Niou, Kaoru, and others float boats on the Uji River for autumn-leaf viewing; women watch from the Eighth Prince's villa.

summaryen: Kaoru arranges a match between Prince Niou and Naka no Kimi, hoping to demonstrate his unselfish devotion to Oigimi. When Niou's visits to Uji slacken due to royal opposition, Oigimi is stricken with guilt over her sister's uncertain fate, falling into fatal melancholy. Maintaining her maidenly refusal to the last, she dies in Kaoru's weeping arms, shattering his spirit.

title: 早蕨
summary: 姉・大君を失い一人宇治に残された中君のもとへ、山の阿闍梨から早春の蕨や土筆が届けられる。薫は後見として心を尽くし、中君を京の二条院にある匂宮の邸へ引き取る手配を進める。姉の喪に服しながら宇治を離れる中君に対し、薫は大君の面影を重ねて恋慕の情を抱き始めるが、中君は京へ移り匂宮の妻としての生活を歩み始める。
gendaibun: 姉の大君がお亡くなりになって後、宇治の山荘にたった一人残された中の君は、明けても暮れても涙に濡れて、悲しみに明け暮れていた。
gendaibunen: After the death of her elder sister Oigimi, Naka no Kimi was left entirely alone at the mountain villa in Uji, spending her days and nights drenched in ceaseless tears.
kobun: 大君失せたまひて後、宇治の館に一人残りたまへる中の君、明かし暮らすにつけても、悲しきこと尽きせず。
kobunen: Left alone at the Uji residence after Oigimi had passed away, Naka no Kimi spent her mornings and evenings in unabated grief.

scene.content: 大君亡きあと、寂しく暮らす中の君のもとに、山の阿闍梨より籠にいれた蕨や土筆が文を添えて贈られる。
scene.contenten: After the eldest sister's death, the mountain acarya sends the lonely middle sister a basket of bracken and horsetails with a letter.

scene.content: 庭前の紅梅を愛でながら箏を掻き鳴らす匂宮のもとを訪れた薫、紅梅の枝を折り、匂宮に歌を詠みかける。
scene.contenten: Visiting Prince Niou, who plucks the koto before the garden's red plums, Kaoru breaks off a red plum branch and recites a poem to him.

scene.content: 京の匂宮のもとへ移る中の君、大君を偲んで悲しむところへ、薫来訪。前に姫君たちをかいまみた障子の穴に寄って見るが、室内は見えない。
scene.contenten: The middle sister, moving to Prince Niou's in the capital, grieves for the eldest; Kaoru visits and looks through the hole in the sliding door where he once glimpsed the princesses, but cannot see inside.

scene.content: 中の君、上洛を前に弁の尼との別れを悲しむ。
scene.contenten: The middle sister grieves over parting with the nun Ben before going up to the capital.

summaryen: Grieving alone in Uji, Naka no Kimi receives fresh bracken shoots from the mountain abbot. Kaoru loyally makes arrangements to relocate her to Niou's Nijo residence in the capital. As she departs Uji, Kaoru glimpses his lost love Oigimi in her and feels an unexpected pang of attraction, but chivalrously delivers her into Niou's protection.

title: 宿木
summary: 匂宮は夕霧の娘・六の君と政略結婚を結び、懐妊中の中君は不安に打ちひしがれる。薫は中君を慰めるうちに思いを打ち明けるが、中君は自らの異母妹・浮舟の存在を薫に示唆してかわす。中君は無事に男子を出産。一方、薫は今上帝の女二の宮と結婚するが大君を忘れられない。初瀬参詣の帰途、宇治に立ち寄った薫は、大君に生き写しの浮舟を偶然垣間見ることになる。
gendaibun: 今上帝は、女二の宮の御婿として薫の右大将をふさわしいとお考えになり、内々にその思し召しを漏らされることがあった。
gendaibunen: The reigning Emperor considered the Right Major General Kaoru to be an ideal match for the Second Princess, privately hinting at his imperial intentions.
kobun: 主上、女二の宮の御婿に、薫の大将を思し召し立ちて、内々に仰せ出づることもありけり。
kobunen: The Emperor favored Major General Kaoru as husband for the Second Princess, letting his intentions be known privately.

scene.content: 女二の宮を薫に降嫁させようと考える帝、薫を碁の相手に召し寄せる。清涼殿東庭の白菊が霜のため色が変わっている頃である。
scene.contenten: The Emperor, thinking to marry the Second Princess to Kaoru, summons Kaoru as a go partner; it is the time when white chrysanthemums in the east garden of the Seiryoden have changed color from frost.

scene.content: 帝、薫に碁の賭物として菊を折らせ、女二の宮降嫁の意を仄めかす。
scene.contenten: The Emperor has Kaoru pluck a chrysanthemum as a go wager and hints at the Second Princess's marriage.

scene.content: 夕霧の六の君との結婚のため、六条院へ出かける匂宮を見送り、中の君憂悶する。
scene.contenten: Seeing off Prince Niou, who sets out for Rokujo-in to marry Yugiri's Sixth Daughter, the middle sister frets.

scene.content: 宇治を訪れた薫より土産として中の君のもとに届けられた山蔦と文を見た匂宮、嫉妬しながらも、わざと返事を書くように勧める。
scene.contenten: Prince Niou, seeing the mountain ivy and letter sent as a gift to the middle sister by Kaoru, who visited Uji, jealously yet deliberately urges her to reply.

scene.content: 匂宮、晩秋の庭を肌に琵琶を弾き、中の君は脇息によって思い悩む。
scene.contenten: Prince Niou plays the biwa in the late-autumn garden, and the middle sister leans on an armrest in distress.

summaryen: Niou contracts a formal alliance with Yugiri's daughter Roku no Kimi, alarming the pregnant Naka no Kimi. While comforting her, Kaoru expresses affection, but she deflects his advances by hinting at her unacknowledged half-sister, Ukifune. Kaoru later accepts marriage with the Emperor's Second Princess, yet remains inconsolable until he accidentally catches sight of Ukifune at Uji, stunned by her likeness to Oigimi.

title: 東屋
summary: 八の宮の落胤である浮舟は継父・常陸介のもとで育つが、実母の中将の君は高貴な身分との良縁を望み異母姉・中君のもとに預ける。二条院で浮舟を見初めた匂宮が強引に迫る事件が起き、驚いた母は浮舟を三条の隠れ家へ連れ戻す。事情を知った薫は三条を訪れて浮舟を引き取り、亡き大君の面影を追い求めて彼女を自らの宇治山荘へと隠す。
gendaibun: 薫の大将は、故大君の面影をいつまでも忘れかねて、あの宇治で垣間見た浮舟の行方を、弁の尼などを通じて熱心に尋ねさせておられた。
gendaibunen: Major General Kaoru, unable to forget the memory of the late Oigimi, inquired persistently through Ben no Ama for news of Ukifune, whom he had glimpsed at Uji.
kobun: 大将の君、かの亡き大君の面影忘れがたくて、宇治に行き通ひたまふついでに、浮舟の御ゆかりを尋ねさせたまふ。
kobunen: General Kaoru, haunted by the lingering memory of the late Oigimi, made inquiries regarding Ukifune whenever he visited Uji.

scene.content: 匂宮、障子を開けて浮舟の裾を捉える。 浮舟、扇をかざしながら宮を振り向き見る。
scene.contenten: Prince Niou opens the sliding door and catches Ukifune's hem; Ukifune turns to look at him, holding up her fan.

scene.content: 中の君、絵を出して浮舟に見せ、右近に物語の詞を読ませる。
scene.contenten: The middle sister brings out pictures to show Ukifune and has Ukon read the text of the tale.

scene.content: 薫、三条の浮舟の隠れ家を訪ね、雨の簀子に待つ。
scene.contenten: Kaoru visits Ukifune's hideaway at Sanjo and waits on the rainy veranda.

scene.content: 三条の隠れ家で一夜を明かした薫、車を妻戸に寄せて浮舟を乗せ宇治に移そうとする。
scene.contenten: Kaoru, having spent the night at the Sanjo hideaway, brings his carriage to the door, takes Ukifune aboard, and tries to move her to Uji.

summaryen: Ukifune, the unrecognized daughter of the Eighth Prince, stays with Naka no Kimi at Nijo, where Prince Niou stumbles upon her and forces an embrace. Terrified, her mother whisks Ukifune to a modest hideout at Sanjo. Informed of her retreat, Kaoru comes for Ukifune and spirits her away to his secluded villa at Uji to serve as a living surrogate for Oigimi.

title: 浮舟
summary: 宇治に隠された浮舟の居所を突き止めた匂宮は、薫を装って宇治山荘に侵入し契りを結ぶ。情熱的な匂宮に浮舟も次第に心を惹かれていく。しかし慎重な薫と情熱的な匂宮という対照的な二人の貴公子から同時に求愛され、浮舟の二股関係は露見寸前に陥る。両者への板挟みと裏切りの自責に耐えかねた浮舟は、夜の宇治川への投身自殺を決意する。
gendaibun: 匂宮は、あの東屋の君（浮舟）が宇治の山荘に隠されていることを突き止められると、何としてももう一度逢いたいとお思いになり、人目を忍んで宇治へ向かわれた。
gendaibunen: Having discovered that the lady Ukifune was concealed at the Uji villa, Prince Niou became determined to meet her once more, setting out in deep disguise for Uji.
kobun: 匂宮、かの東屋の君の、宇治におはします処を聞き出ださせたまひて、いかでまづ逢はむと思し召し立つ。
kobunen: Prince Niou, having learned that the maiden of the Azumaya was kept at Uji, resolved to go and contrive a meeting at once.

scene.content: 正月、中の君のもとで若君をあやし遊ぶ匂宮。そこへ、居所を隠している浮舟よりの文をつけた小松と髭籠を持った女童が走って来る。
scene.contenten: At New Year Prince Niou plays with the young lord at the middle sister's; a girl running with a small pine and a basket attached to a letter from Ukifune, who is hiding her whereabouts, arrives.

scene.content: 匂宮、忍んで宇治の浮舟を訪ね、隙間より室内を覗く。浮舟は縫物をする女たちの間に臥す。
scene.contenten: Prince Niou steals to visit Ukifune at Uji and peeks inside through a gap; Ukifune lies among the women sewing.

scene.content: 春の日を浮舟とともに過ごす匂宮、男女が寄り添って乱している絵を描いて浮舟に見せる。
scene.contenten: Prince Niou, spending a spring day with Ukifune, draws a picture of a man and woman lying close together and shows it to her.

scene.content: 雪の中、匂宮、浮舟を小舟に乗せて宇治川を渡り、橘の小島で愛を誓う。
scene.contenten: In the snow Prince Niou sets Ukifune in a small boat, crosses the Uji River, and pledges love on the tangerine islet.

scene.content: 夜、宇治に忍んだ匂宮、薫の命で警戒が厳しく邸に入れず、野原に侍従を呼び出して逢う。
scene.contenten: At night Prince Niou, stealing into Uji, cannot enter the residence because Kaoru has set strict guards, and calls a lady out to the field to meet.

summaryen: Discovering Ukifune's location, Niou disguises himself as Kaoru, gains entrance to the Uji villa, and seduces her. Ukifune finds herself swayed by Niou's fiery ardor while remaining indebted to Kaoru's serene constancy. Torn between the two competing noblemen and seeing discovery inevitable, the guilt-ridden Ukifune flees into the dark to drown herself in the turbulent Uji River.

title: 蜻蛉
summary: 浮舟の失踪に気づいた宇治の女房たちは投水自殺と覚り、世間体を恐れて遺骸のないまま密かに荼毘に付して葬儀を済ませる。訃報を聞いた薫と匂宮はそれぞれ狂乱し悲嘆に暮れる。薫は四十九日法要を手厚く営むが、やがて夏、匂宮の妻・女一の宮の涼やかな美しさに惹かれ、空虚な心に蜻蛉のように儚い命の無常を感じる。
gendaibun: 宇治の山荘では、浮舟の姫君が跡形もなく消え失せてしまわれたので、女房たちは慌て惑い、川へ身を投げられたに違いないと泣き叫んだ。
gendaibunen: At the Uji villa, Princess Ukifune had vanished without a trace, throwing her gentlewomen into utter panic as they wept in certainty that she had cast herself into the river.
kobun: 宇治の館には、姫君の行方失せたまひぬるを、人々あわて惑ひて、川に入りたまひぬるにやと、泣き叫ぶ。
kobunen: In the Uji residence, the ladies were thrown into chaos over the Princess's disappearance, crying out in grief that she must have thrown herself into the torrent.

scene.content: 薫、 前庭の橘の花が香るなかで時鳥の鳴き渡るのを聞く。
scene.contenten: Kaoru hears a cuckoo calling as the tangerine flowers in the front garden scent the air.

scene.content: 夏の夕暮れ、薄物を着た女一の宮や女房ら、氷をもって涼むようすを薫覗き見る。
scene.contenten: On a summer evening Kaoru peeks at the First Princess and the ladies in thin robes cooling themselves with ice.

scene.content: 女一の宮の美しさに立ち去りがたい思いの薫、下使いの女房が引き返して来るのに気付き、身を隠す。
scene.contenten: Kaoru, reluctant to leave the First Princess's beauty, notices a lower servant woman turning back and hides himself.

scene.content: 薫、昨日垣間見た女一の宮と同じ紅の羅の単衣を縫わせ、几帳に掛け置いたのを手ずから女二の宮に着せようとする。
scene.contenten: Kaoru has a crimson silk robe like the one of the First Princess he glimpsed yesterday sewn and hung on a screen, and tries to dress the Second Princess in it himself.

scene.content: 薫、夕暮れに飛び交う蜻蛉を見て、大君や浮舟とのはかない縁を思う。
scene.contenten: Kaoru watches dragonflies flitting at dusk and thinks of his fleeting ties with the eldest sister and Ukifune.

summaryen: Discovering Ukifune's footwear by the water, her distraught attendants stage a sham funeral to hide her drowning. Both Kaoru and Niou are overwhelmed with agony upon receiving news of her death. Kaoru sponsors lavish memorial rites, but in summer catches a glimpse of the First Princess, meditating forlornly on the ephemerality of human existence like flitting dragonflies.

title: 手習
summary: 川辺で気を失っていた浮舟は、比叡山横川の僧都によって奇跡的に救出され小野の庵で保護されていた。記憶を取り戻した浮舟は俗世の愛執を断ち切るため、反対する僧都に懇願して髪を下ろし受戒する。小野の山里で念仏と手習いに明け暮れる中、明石中宮の加持に訪れた僧都の噂話から、薫は死んだはずの浮舟が生きていることを確信する。
gendaibun: 初瀬参詣の帰途、宇治川のほとりで倒れていた女を助けられた横川の僧都は、比叡の小野の庵室へ連れ帰って手厚く介抱しておられた。
gendaibunen: The Prelate of Yokawa, who had rescued an unconscious woman lying beside the Uji River on his way back from Hase, brought her to a hermitage in Ono and cared for her attentively.
kobun: 初瀬より帰る道に、宇治川の辺に倒れ臥したる人を見つけて、横川の僧都、小野の庵に連れ帰りて介抱しきこゆ。
kobunen: Finding a prostrate woman lying near the banks of the Uji River on his return from Hase, the Prelate of Yokawa brought her back to his hermitage at Ono and ministered to her.

scene.content: 宇治院の木の下に倒れ伏す浮舟を僧たち発見。
scene.contenten: Monks discover Ukifune lying collapsed beneath a tree at the Uji monastery.

scene.content: 僧都ら、妹尼の頼みで山を下り、一夜浮舟を加持する。
scene.contenten: The bishop and others, at the younger nun's request, come down the mountain and perform incantations over Ukifune for a night.

scene.content: 秋、浮舟が身を寄せる小野の君の庵の前で、稲を刈る人々、歌を歌い興じあう。
scene.contenten: In autumn, before the hermitage of Lady Ono where Ukifune stays, people harvesting rice sing songs merrily.

scene.content: 浮舟、少将のに誘われて碁を打つ。
scene.contenten: Ukifune plays go at the Shosho's invitation.

scene.content: 尼君の庵に立ち寄った僧都に、浮舟出家したいと願い、几帳の帷子の綻びより髪を掻き出して切ってもらおうとする。
scene.contenten: To the bishop who stops at the nun's hermitage, Ukifune expresses her wish to take the tonsure and tries to have him cut her hair through a tear in the screen curtain.

scene.content: 髪を下ろした浮舟、一人硯に向かい手習いをする。
scene.contenten: Ukifune, having taken the tonsure, sits alone at the inkstone practicing calligraphy.

summaryen: Rescued from the verge of death by the holy Prelate of Yokawa, Ukifune is nursed back to health at a nunnery in Ono. Longing to sever all ties with worldly romance, she begs the prelate to administer the tonsure. Living as a novice practicing calligraphy, her existence is eventually disclosed to Kaoru when the prelate speaks of her during an exorcism service for the Empress.

title: 夢浮橋
summary: 浮舟の生存を確信した薫は横川の僧都を訪ねて真偽を確かめ、浮舟の異父弟・小君を使者として小野の庵へ文を届ける。小君から薫の手紙を差し出された浮舟は激しく動揺するが、かつての愛執に立ち戻ることを恐れ、「人違いでしょう」と言下に面会も返書も拒絶する。戻った小君から報告を受けた薫は、誰か別の男が彼女を隠しているのではないかという疑念に苛まれながら立ち尽くす。
gendaibun: 薫の大将は横川の僧都を密かに訪ねられ、宇治川で助けられた女の素性について詳しく確かめられた。
gendaibunen: Major General Kaoru secretly visited the Prelate of Yokawa, inquiring closely into the identity of the woman who had been rescued from the Uji River.
kobun: 薫の大将、横川の僧都を訪ねたまひて、かの宇治川の辺にて助けたまへりけむ人の御ことを、委しく尋ねきこえたまふ。
kobunen: General Kaoru visited the Prelate of Yokawa, inquiring minutely into the circumstances of the lady who had been saved by the Uji River.

scene.content: 薫、横川の僧都を訪ね、浮舟入水後の事情を聞き、浮舟の弟の小君に文を届けさせるようにと頼む。
scene.contenten: Kaoru visits the bishop of Yokawa, hears the circumstances after Ukifune's immersion, and asks him to have Ukifune's younger brother Kogimi deliver a letter.

scene.content: 浮舟のいる小野の里の遥か向こうの谷を、薫の立派な行列が通る。 尼たちそれを眺める。
scene.contenten: Kaoru's fine procession passes the valley far beyond the Ono village where Ukifune lives; the nuns watch it.

scene.content: 小君、薫の文を小野の庵室に届け、尼君開いて浮舟にみせる。
scene.contenten: Kogimi delivers Kaoru's letter to the hermitage at Ono; the nun opens it and shows it to Ukifune.

summaryen: Learning Ukifune lives, Kaoru sends her younger half-brother Kogimi to her retreat at Ono with an urgent letter. Deeply shaken yet terrified of rekindling tragic passions, the nun Ukifune turns Kogimi away, claiming he has mistaken her for someone else and refusing even to open the missive. When Kogimi returns empty-handed, Kaoru is left suspended in torment, wondering if another lover has concealed her.
